tasks.short: Sell tickets and other items at the till to customers.

steps.what: Ask customers which tickets or other items they want
Find those tickets or items on the till
Confirm the price and the items with customers
Take payment and complete the sale of the tickets
Hand the tickets or other items to customers

tasks.design: Preset keys and barcodes on the {OTHER} till (the point-of-sale register) fill the sale line for tickets and other items. The cashier still confirms the line with the customer, takes card or cash on the {BANK} terminal, and hands the tickets over. Tender buttons only shorten keying.
tasks.previous_blocker: Ticket types lived in a paper price list or a long till code list, so each sale meant a search while the customer waited.
tasks.enabler_now: The till already stores items and barcodes. Loading ticket types as buttons is configuration, not a new system.
tasks.still_hard: A ticket that is not in the catalogue, a price override, and cash in the drawer still need the cashier at the counter.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier hears which performance or item the customer means when the name is vague, and says the price before money moves.
tasks.altitude: The cashier still sells at the counter all day. Code searches get shorter. They do not gain a new right to change prices; overrides stay on the existing till permission.

reach.task: quote a rental charge before taking payment
reach.learn: which price fields must be on the till before anyone tells the customer a figure

evidence.claim: A retail till can store item buttons and barcodes so the cashier selects a ticket type instead of searching a code list.

assumptions: Workflow boundary is the counter sale: from the customer's request to the tickets in their hand. Stock replenishment and event seating maps are out of scope.

Structured input is the item catalogue on the {OTHER} till: item code, name, price, tax code, barcode. The store's retail lead produces it. If a ticket has no code, the cashier types the amount as today.
Routine card and cash taking stays with the cashier. No second approver is added for an ordinary sale.
No per-cashier speed score is stored.
unknowns: Whether ticket types already exist as till items or only on paper.
Who may change a price, and the override limit.
research_questions: What share of ticket sales are barcode or preset, and what share are open-price?
Does the till already receive the item file from the web shop, or is it keyed by hand?

already_counted.description: Cashier still checks the sale line shows the tickets or items the customer named.

incremental.description: Keep ticket types, prices and barcodes current on the till when the range changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of the task is the conversation, the payment and handing tickets over, which stay. Only the code search shrinks, and less so when barcodes already exist. Two hours of catalogue upkeep per 100 baseline hours are deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Bag, box or gift-wrap merchandise and prepare packages for shipment.

steps.what: Hear if merchandise needs a bag, a box or a shipment
Bag, box or gift-wrap the merchandise by hand
Prepare packages by sealing them and writing the address
Prepare the shipment label from the package address
Release the shipment after the label matches the package
Hand the wrapped merchandise or the shipment to customers

tasks.design: Bagging, gift-wrap and sealing stay in the cashier's hands. When the delivery address is already name, street, postcode and country, the {OPS_SYSTEM} fills a carrier label. The cashier reads that label against the package and only then releases the booking. A spoken address is still typed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The address was spoken or handwritten, and the carrier screen was a separate site, so the till could not fill the label.
tasks.enabler_now: Carrier booking from structured address fields is a fixed call. The till can store those fields when the customer gives them at the sale.
tasks.still_hard: Wrapping, weighing odd shapes, and reading a bad handwritten address stay manual. A wrong postcode still sends the package away.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier sees that the label names the same person and street as the package in front of them.
tasks.altitude: The week is still wrapping and the counter. The cashier keeps the right to stop a shipment. They do not take on carrier contract negotiations.

reach.task: pack a part that must leave the same day
reach.learn: which address fields have to exist before a label is worth printing

evidence.claim: Booking a shipment and printing a label from structured address fields is a deterministic carrier integration. The group digest treats shipping cost and tracking that way, without a named product.

assumptions: Workflow boundary is the counter package: from the wrap request to the package in the customer's hands or the carrier pickup. Line-haul and customs are out of scope.
Structured input is delivery name, street, postcode, city, country and service code, produced by the cashier from the customer or copied from the sale. Fallback is typing the label as today.
Screen time today is a small slice of this task. Wrapping is not given an invented system share.
The label release approves shipment-label-draft for that package. A changed address voids it.
Carrier account access is a store credential, not a new staff-monitoring tool.
unknowns: Whether this store ships from the counter or only bags and gift-wraps.
Which carrier, and whether the address is captured on the sale or only spoken.
research_questions: What share of packages have a full address on the sale before wrapping starts?
Who pays the carrier charge, the customer at the till or a store account?

already_counted.description: Cashier still checks the drafted label text against the package.
Cashier still spends the release step reading the label and confirming the booking.

incremental.description: Maintain carrier service codes and the label field mapping when the carrier changes them.

approvals.approved_version: shipment-label-draft matched to the sealed package address

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Wrapping, sealing and handover stay fully manual. Only label typing shrinks, and only when the address was already structured. Spoken addresses are retyped. Carrier-code upkeep is deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Cash checks for customers after matching identity and the paper.

steps.what: Take the paper and ask customers for identification
Read the amount and payee on customers' checks into the till

loop.input: photo of the paper check and the machine-read code line
loop.output: amount, date, payee and account as fields
loop.check: the cashier compares the extracted amount and payee with the handwriting on the paper; a mismatch is rejected
loop.stop: one extraction attempt, then the cashier types the fields; no second call
loop.why_not_simpler: the written amount and payee are handwriting, not a fixed export from the till

steps.what: Draft the payout from the checks and the identity match
Decide and count cash out for customers' checks
File the endorsed checks and the payout slip

tasks.design: A bounded read on the {OTHER} till (the check reader) proposes amount, date and payee from the paper. The cashier compares that with the handwriting, applies the store limit, and only then counts out cash against the payout draft. A refusal is never produced by the reader alone. The image and the slip go to {DOCS} for the finance team.
tasks.previous_blocker: The written amount and the payee do not sit in a field the till can trust, and paying the wrong cash is hard to reverse.
tasks.enabler_now: The code line is machine-readable, and one bounded read can propose the handwritten fields for the cashier to accept or retype.
tasks.still_hard: Forged checks, a payee that does not match the identification, and counting the notes stay with the cashier. The store's limit and the bank's willingness to take the check are not in the model.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier decides whether this check should be cashed, and counts the notes into the customer's hand.
tasks.altitude: The cashier still owns the cash-out decision on every check. They spend less time retyping a clear amount. They do not gain authority to raise the store limit.

reach.role: gambling change person and booth cashier
reach.task: pay cash against a voucher the customer presents
reach.learn: which document fields a person must match before cash leaves the drawer

evidence.claim: GDPR article 22 bars a decision based solely on automated processing that has a significant effect on a person.
A check's code line can be read by a device, while the handwritten amount and payee still need a person to compare them with the paper.

assumptions: Workflow boundary is one check at the counter: from the paper and identification to cash in the customer's hand and the check filed. Bank deposit of the day's checks is a finance task.

Structured input is amount, date, payee, account line, identity document type and number, and the store cashing limit. The cashier produces the sighting. If the read mismatches the handwriting, the cashier types the fields and the draft is rebuilt.
The payout approves payout-draft for that check image and amount. Any change to the amount voids it. No solely automated refusal.
Check images are customer financial data. Access is limited to the cashier on shift and the finance team. This design does not score cashiers.

National rules on check cashing and works-council consent for a new till tool vary. The digest names the Dutch works-council statute for staff-monitoring tools; this design avoids a per-cashier score, and the customer must confirm whether consent is still required.
unknowns: Whether this store cashes checks at all, and the amount limit.
Whether identification numbers may be stored or only sighted.
Who in finance receives the filed check, and how often.
research_questions: What share of checks are refused, and for which reason?
Is the code line already read by the till, or is every field typed?

already_counted.description: Cashier still compares the extracted amount and payee with the handwriting.
Cashier still reviews the payout draft against the limit and the identity sighting.
Cashier still checks the filed image matches the endorsed paper check.

incremental.description: Maintain cashing limits, accepted identity types and the reader field mapping, and handle unreadable checks.

approvals.approved_version: payout-draft bound to the check image, amount and identity sighting

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Counting cash and the accept-or-refuse decision stay. The reader helps only on clear handwriting; many checks are still typed. Filing the paper shrinks only a little. Limit and template upkeep is deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Offer customers carry-out service when the transaction is complete.

steps.what: At completion, notice what customers must carry
Check the completed transactions before you offer help
Offer customers carry-out service in person
Carry goods out when customers accept the service

tasks.design: At completion the {OTHER} till shows a bulky-sale flag from item size already on the catalogue. The cashier still looks at the customer, still offers carry-out, and still carries the goods. The flag only shortens re-reading the receipt. It does not record a score for the cashier.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing on the till said the sale was bulky, so the offer depended on the cashier noticing bags at a busy moment.
tasks.enabler_now: Item records can hold a bulky marker, and the till can show it when the transaction completes. That is configuration.
tasks.still_hard: The offer is a spoken judgement, and carrying goods to the door is physical. A flag cannot see a pram or a walking aid.
tasks.human_edge: The cashier sees whether this customer actually needs help, and does the carrying.

ambition.what: customers with a pram or a walking aid who need the purchase taken to the door, not only customers who ask

tasks.altitude: The cashier's week is unchanged in shape: they still offer and still carry. The flag is a reminder, not a new permission. They can ignore it.

reach.task: help a customer move a bulky purchase from the door to the car
reach.learn: which item markers are worth a prompt and which needs only the person's eyes

evidence.claim: A till can show a message at the end of a sale from a marker already stored on the item. It cannot judge whether the customer needs help.

assumptions: Workflow boundary is the end of a sale already rung up: from noticing the load to goods at the door. The sale itself is the ticket-and-item task, not this one.
Structured input is a bulky marker on the item (yes or no), produced by the retail lead on the catalogue. Items without a marker never raise the flag; the cashier still looks.
The flag is not stored as a per-cashier compliance score. If a later design logged who offered carry-out, national works-council rules could treat that as staff monitoring; this design does not.
Upkeep is the bulky marker list, half an hour per 100 baseline hours of this task.
unknowns: Whether item records have a size or bulky field today.
Whether carry-out is store policy or only a courtesy the cashier chooses.
research_questions: How often is carry-out offered today, and how often is it accepted?
Would the works council treat a till prompt as a monitoring tool even without a stored score?

already_counted.description: Cashier still glances at the till flag or the receipt before offering.

incremental.description: Keep the bulky marker current when new items are added to the catalogue.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The offer and the carrying stay. Only re-reading the receipt shrinks, and only when the bulky marker is present and right. Marker upkeep is deducted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The cashier stays on the till and the floor. Ticket codes and clear check amounts take less retyping. Wrapping, cash in the drawer, the check decision and carrying goods out stay theirs. They gain no new authority over prices, limits or carrier contracts.
reach: Counter clerks quoting a price can reuse the same preset-key habit.
Parts salespeople packing a same-day dispatch need the same address fields before a label.
Booth cashiers paying a voucher can copy the rule that cash moves only after a person matches the document.
skills_to_grow: Comparing a check's handwriting with a till extract before any cash moves
Reading a carrier label against the package in hand
Judging when a customer needs goods carried, including when they do not ask
role.ambitious_version: The till holds ticket prices, a bulky marker and a check limit. The cashier's remaining work is the counter itself: understanding the request, refusing a bad check, stopping a wrong label, and carrying goods for someone who needs it.
